comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting for Third-Party Research in Soft-Dollar Arrangements
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm provides third-party research services to clients via soft-dollar arrangements, where incurred research costs are presented net within commissions and fees.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Goldman Sachs disclose third-party arrangements within commissions and fees but apply opposite gross vs. net presentation policies. Citi acts as principal in third-party advisory and custodian transactions, presenting amounts paid to these third parties gross in Transactional and tax charges. In contrast, Goldman Sachs presents third-party research costs incurred in soft-dollar arrangements net within commissions and fees.

sentences.text: In some instances, the Company contracts with third-party advisors and with third-party custodians.
The Company has determined that it acts as principal in the majority of these transactions and therefore presents the amounts paid to third parties gross within Transactional and tax charges.
The firm also provides third-party research services to clients in connection with certain soft-dollar arrangements.
Third-party research costs incurred by the firm in connection with such arrangements are presented net within commissions and fees.

comparisons.peer_summary: Brokerage commissions are collected and recognized as revenue upon the occurrence of the client transaction. The Firm nets certain costs paid to third-party clearing houses and exchanges against this commission revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan Chase disclose the use of third parties in transactional services but differ in how costs are presented relative to revenue. Citi contracts with third-party advisors and custodians and generally acts as principal, presenting amounts paid to third parties gross. JPMorgan Chase facilitates client transactions and nets certain costs paid to third-party clearing houses and exchanges against commission revenue.
